The Damagaram page, which has the same capital move in 1736, also has the Bornu nobles conquer Zinder among the Sassebaki sultanates in the 1830s; the two statements are not reconciled. Founded in 1731 "near Mirriah" by Muslim aristocrats led by Mallam; the page gives no early area, so a 50 km disc round Zinder stands for it at confidence 1. Damagaram was at first "a vassal state of the decaying Borno" (the Bornu dossier's ledger should carry it).

keyframe_review.note: In the 1830s "the small band of Bornu nobles and retainers conquered the Myrria kingdom", along with the Sassebaki sultanates, Zinder among them; the mid-19th-century size was "about 70,000 km2" (travellers' estimate). A 150 km disc round Zinder matches that area. Tanimoune "declared independence" from Bornu in the mid-to-late 19th century (Zinder page) and expanded vigorously.

notes:
Damagaram, additions batch af-03-x; Cliopatria has no row. Pages: Sultanate of Damagaram, Zinder (Battle of Tirmini did not load).

Three internal tensions on the pages: the capital is moved to Zinder in 1736 (both pages), yet the 1830s conquest takes the Sassebaki sultanate of Zinder; the founder's reign is 1736-1743 in the text and 1731-1746 in the ruler list; the sultan Tanimoune's independence from Bornu is only "mid-to-late 19th century". The vassal period under Bornu belongs in the Bornu (empire-of-kanem) ledger and is not recorded here. The 70,000 km2 area is the page's estimate for the mid-19th century and sets the 150 km disc radius; the early disc (50 km) has no support on the page and is at confidence 1. French rule: Marius Cazemajou was killed in Zinder in 1897; the Niger Military Territory had its capital at Zinder in 1911 and Niamey from 1926. The "puppet sultan" of 1906 and the restoration of 1923 are noted, not ledgered.
Gazetteer: Mirriah, Tirmini, Birini, Myrria, Sassebaki.
